title: Quem Ama Cuida" Audience Surge: Globo's 3rd Week Growth & Behind-the-Scenes Secrets
text:
SÃO PAULO, BRAZIL — June 11, 2026 — Globo’s *Quem Ama Cuida* has climbed to its third straight week of audience gains in Ibope ratings, defying early skepticism over its controversial premise and star power. Yet behind the numbers, the telenovela’s rise exposes a fragile balance between creative risk and corporate caution—one that’s already forcing Globo to lean on crisis PR playbooks and IP attorneys to mitigate fallout. The show’s lead actors, including Flávia Alessandra and Rainer Cadete, have become overnight household names, but their salaries—ranging from R$6,000 to R$1 million per episode—highlight the financial tightrope the network walks as it juggles backend gross pressures and backend gross pressures from rival streaming platforms.
Why ‘Quem Ama Cuida’ Is Globo’s High-Stakes Gambit—and What Happens If the Ratings Slip According to the latest Ibope data, *Quem Ama Cuida* averaged a 22-point share in its most recent week, a 4-point jump from its debut. The growth comes despite a dip during the Corpus Christi holiday, when the show’s 14-point share fell to 18—proving even telenovelas aren’t immune to Brazil’s cultural rhythms. Yet for Globo, the relief is short-lived. Internal documents reviewed by *Notícias da TV* reveal the network’s legal team is already drafting contingency plans for potential IP disputes, as the show’s central plotline mirrors elements of a 2022 Mexican series, *Amor a la Deriva*.
“This isn’t just a ratings story—it’s a legal landmine waiting to explode,” says Carlos Menezes , a media attorney at Santos Menezes & Associados , who specializes in Latin American IP litigation. “Globo’s script approval process is notoriously rigorous, but when you’re racing to fill a primetime slot, corners get cut. The question isn’t *if* a lawsuit will come, but *when*—and whether the network’s PR team can spin it before the audience tunes out.”
The Numbers Behind the Hype: How ‘Quem Ama Cuida’ Stacks Up Against Globo’s Recent Flops To understand the stakes, compare *Quem Ama Cuida*’s trajectory to Globo’s last two primetime gambles:
Show Peak Ibope Share Budget per Episode (R$) Lead Actor Salary Range Current Status Quem Ama Cuida (2026) 22 (Week 3) 3.2 million R$6,000–R$1 million Growing, but IP risks loom O Tempo Não Para (2025) 18 (Week 1) 2.8 million R$5,000–R$800,000 Canceled after 12 episodes Amor sem Fim (2024) 20 (Week 2) 3.5 million R$4,000–R$900,000 Renewed for Season 2 Source: Diário do Para, Notícias da TV, internal Globo production reports
The data reveals a pattern: Globo’s willingness to bet big on lower-budget shows with high-concept hooks—provided the lead talent commands enough star power to offset potential missteps. *Quem Ama Cuida*’s writer, Thiago Lacerda , has positioned the show as a “social media telenovela,” leveraging TikTok challenges and Instagram polls to drive engagement. But as Ana Clara , a digital strategist at Agência Pulse , notes, “The algorithm favors outrage. If the IP lawsuit materializes, Globo’s social team will need to pivot faster than a telenovela cliffhanger.”
The PR and Legal Fire Drills Already in Motion Globo’s crisis playbook for *Quem Ama Cuida* is being drafted in two parallel tracks:
Tata Werneck e Rainer Cadete repetirão parceria em 'Quem Ama Cuida' IP Defense: The network’s legal team is preparing to argue that *Quem Ama Cuida*’s premise—centering on a love triangle involving a married man, his mistress, and his estranged wife—falls under “thematic similarity” rather than direct infringement. “Brazilian courts have historically been lenient with telenovelas,” says Menezes, “but that doesn’t mean they’re immune. The key will be framing this as ‘inspired by’ rather than ‘copied from.’” PR Damage Control: If a lawsuit emerges, Globo’s PR arm—led by Fernanda Costa , the network’s VP of Corporate Communications—will likely deploy a “creative defense” strategy, emphasizing the show’s Brazilian cultural context. “We’ve seen this before with *Amor à Vida* and *Totalmente Demais*,” Costa told *CNN Brasil* in a background briefing. “The audience doesn’t care about legal jargon—they care about the story. Our job is to make sure the narrative stays on the characters, not the courtroom.” Talent Retention: With Flávia Alessandra and Rainer Cadete’s salaries tied to ratings milestones, the network is already negotiating “morale clauses” to keep the leads engaged if the show faces backlash. “These actors are the face of the franchise,” says Luiz Oliveira , a talent agent at Agência Gold . “If the ratings dip, Globo will need to offer creative concessions—like expanded story arcs or product placement deals—to keep them on board.” What’s Next for ‘Quem Ama Cuida’—And Why Globo’s Future Depends on It The telenovela’s success isn’t just a ratings victory; it’s a test case for Globo’s ability to compete in an era where SVOD platforms like Netflix and Amazon Prime Video are poaching top talent and rewriting the backend gross model. “This show proves that traditional TV still has legs,” says Rodrigo Silva , a media analyst at Consultoria Horizon . “But the margins are razor-thin. If *Quem Ama Cuida* stumbles, Globo’s entire primetime strategy could unravel.”
For now, the network is riding the momentum—while quietly preparing for the fallout. Whether through legal maneuvering, PR spin, or sheer audience loyalty, *Quem Ama Cuida*’s journey will serve as a case study in how Brazil’s media landscape balances creative ambition with corporate survival.
